briefings.title: Full Interview: Bill Gurley Thinks College Kills Creativity
briefings.tldr: True career success stems from "high agency" and hyper-curiosity, traits that allow individuals to utilize AI as a professional superpower rather than a displacement threat in an increasingly competitive and regulated economic landscape.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
True career success stems from "high agency" and hyper-curiosity, traits that allow individuals to utilize AI as a professional superpower rather than a displacement threat in an increasingly competitive and regulated economic landscape.

## The Philosophy of "High Agency" and Career Development
* **Rejecting Restrictive Pathways:** Gurley argues that the modern college system has become too rigid, forcing students into narrow majors and stifling the exploration necessary to find true obsession or "life’s work."
    * **The "Late Bloomer" Reality:** Gurley emphasizes that many successful founders (e.g., Enzo Ferrari, Estée Lauder) did not find their path until their 30s or 40s. Gurley himself did not enter venture capital until age 30.
* **The Power of Knowledge:** While talent is innate, Gurley posits that being the most knowledgeable person in a room is a choice.
    * **Information Accessibility:** In the current era, there is "no excuse" for lack of knowledge because all necessary information is available at one's fingertips.
* **Curiosity as a Differentiator:** The most successful individuals are those who cannot "sleep on not knowing something" and maintain a hyper-curiosity that borders on paranoia regarding new developments.

## The AI Paradox: Threat vs. Superpower
* **Agency as the Deciding Factor:** Gurley identifies a sharp divide in how AI is perceived:
    * **The Threat:** For those unengaged in their work or following a standard path, AI feels like a replacement.
    * **The Superpower:** For "high-agency" individuals, AI acts as a force multiplier for self-learning, networking, and productivity.
* **The Nature of the AI Bubble:** Gurley clarifies that bubbles are often born from reality rather than fiction.
    * **"Fools Rush In":** Because AI is demonstrably "real" (like the Gold Rush), it attracts speculators and charlatans, leading to inevitable market resets. 
    * **Index Exposure:** He suggests that retail investors seeking AI exposure are often better served by owning standard indices (containing Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet) rather than chasing high-priced private placement SPVs.

## Shifting Dynamics in Venture Capital (VC)
* **The "Hijacking" of Growth:** Large funds are now massive enough to keep companies like Stripe or Databricks private for much longer than in previous cycles.
    * **Public Market Decline:** This trend deprives public investors of the high-growth years that companies like Amazon offered when they went public at valuations below $1B.
* **The Retail Risk:** Gurley is skeptical of opening VC to retail investors, noting that the "Power Law" (where 7 out of 10 investments fail) is often incompatible with retail risk tolerance and the lack of audited transparency in private startups.
* **The Regulatory Bottleneck:** He points to high costs of being public, including SEC scrutiny and D&O insurance, as the primary reasons companies avoid IPOs, effectively halving the number of public US companies over time.

## Geopolitics and Regulatory Capture
* **The Open Source Threat:** Gurley warns that the biggest threat to US AI dominance isn't just Chinese innovation, but the global adoption of Chinese open-source models.
* **Regulatory Capture Risks:** He expresses concern that US labs (like OpenAI and Anthropic) are lobbying for heavy regulation to protect their positions.
    * **The "Fence" Scenario:** If the US over-regulates, it may inadvertently create a digital fence around itself, allowing China to serve the rest of the global market with more accessible models.
* **VC "Warmongering":** Gurley observes a shift in the VC community toward defense and military technology (e.g., Anduril), noting the irony that many investors who previously criticized "warmongers" are now heavily allocated to the sector.

## Notable Quotes

> "I can’t make you the most talented person in your company or your group or your field, but you have no excuse not to be the most knowledgeable person because the information’s all out there." — **Bill Gurley**

> "For high-agency people who are kind of on their own custom career path... AI’s like a superpower. There’s never, ever, ever in the history of the world been a better time to self-learn." — **Bill Gurley**

> "The fact that [AI] is real causes the bubble and that’s why fools rush in. I mean, the beginning of the gold rush, there was really gold there... At the end, it got speculative." — **Bill Gurley**

> "If we get super heavy on US regulation, you may find there’s a fence around the US and China serves the rest of the world. That’s what I’d be worried about." — **Bill Gurley**

briefings.title: HSBC CEO Elhedery on Earnings, HK Property & AI Strategy | Insight with Haslinda Amin 02/25/2026
briefings.tldr: HSBC reported a strong 2025 pre-tax profit of $29.9 billion, beating expectations and driving a 14% dividend increase.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
HSBC reported a strong 2025 pre-tax profit of $29.9 billion, beating expectations and driving a 14% dividend increase. CEO Georges Elhedery signaled an accelerated restructuring timeline, targeting a return on tangible equity (RoTE) of 17% or higher through 2028 while navigating Hong Kong commercial real estate cycles and integrating Generative AI.

## Financial Performance and 2028 Roadmap
*   **Earnings Excellence:** HSBC posted a $29.9 billion pre-tax profit for 2025, driven largely by its wealth management division and Asia-focused strategy.
    *   **Shareholder Returns:** Increased dividends by 14% to $0.75 per share; stock price has risen nearly 90% since Elhedery took office in 2024.
*   **Medium-Term Targets:** The bank has upgraded its guidance for the 2026–2028 period.
    *   **Revenue Growth:** Targeted to rise annually, reaching 5% by 2028.
    *   **Profitability:** Targeted Return on Tangible Equity (RoTE) of 17% or higher for each of the next three years.
*   **Investment Focus:** Capital is being prioritized for "powerhouse" regions including Wealth in Asia and the Middle East, alongside transaction banking to capture shifting supply chain corridors.

## Restructuring and Strategic M&A
*   **Hang Seng Privatization:** The bank completed the privatization of Hang Seng Bank ahead of schedule.
    *   **Synergy Targets:** Management anticipates a $0.9 billion upside by the end of 2028, split evenly between cost reductions and revenue synergies.
*   **Organizational Simplification:** Elhedery expects to conclude major reorganization decisions by June 2026, six months ahead of the original plan.
    *   **Portfolio Cleanup:** The bank continues to exit non-strategic or low-returning activities to reallocate capital toward high-growth corridors.
*   **M&A Discipline:** Future acquisitions must meet four strict criteria:
    *   1. Alignment with core strategy.
    *   2. Delivery of significant scale or capabilities.
    *   3. No distraction from organic growth.
    *   4. Greater accretion than a share buyback.

## Hong Kong Outlook and Real Estate Risks
*   **Commercial Real Estate (CRE) Headwinds:** HSBC booked a $700 million charge related to Hong Kong and Chinese CRE. 
    *   **Cyclical View:** Elhedery characterized the CRE slump as a standard cycle, noting signs of "normalization" in the residential sector and easing pressure from declining interest rates.
*   **Hong Kong as a Global Hub:** Management maintains a "strong conviction" in Hong Kong, predicting it will become the world's largest cross-border wealth hub by 2030.
*   **Government Policy:** Concurrent Hong Kong budget reports forecast 2.5%–3.5% GDP growth for 2026, with new tax incentives to attract family offices and digital asset investments.

## AI Integration and Workforce Strategy
*   **GenAI Deployment:** HSBC is diffusing AI through three streams: productivity tools for all staff, specialized coding assistants, and large-scale "future-proofing" training.
*   **Hiring Impacts:** Despite AI advancements, Elhedery stated that human judgment remains irreplaceable for accountability and audit.
    *   **Entry-Level Talent:** The bank maintains its commitment to hiring 1,500–1,600 graduates annually.
*   **Compensation Philosophy:** Following a 10% increase in the bonus pool, the bank is moving toward a highly differentiated compensation structure to reward top-tier performance and embed a "high-performance culture."

## Global Macroeconomic Context
*   **U.S. Policy Shifts:** President Trump’s State of the Union emphasized a commitment to unilateral tariffs as an economic and national security tool, bypassing Congress where necessary.
*   **Geopolitical Risks:** The administration signaled potential military/economic escalations regarding Iran, citing recent operations in Venezuela as a template for "successful" intervention.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "We are transforming with precision, with discipline, and we're doing it at pace... we expect to be able to conclude a number of the actions we set out to do earlier than initially planned." — **Georges Elhedery**, HSBC CEO

> "The accountability of everything we do remains with humans. We believe in strong controls, we believe in strong resilience... human judgment, I don't see it as being replaced in the short term." — **Georges Elhedery**, HSBC CEO

> "I used these tariffs to take in hundreds of billions of dollars to make great deals for our country, both economically and on a national security basis." — **Donald Trump**, President of the United States (via transcript)

briefings.title: How We Built a $159B Company as Brothers
briefings.tldr: Stripe reported 34% year-over-year growth, driven by a "phase transition" in 2025 and 2026 where new AI-native business cohorts are launching faster and performing better than any previous group in the company’s history.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Stripe reported 34% year-over-year growth, driven by a "phase transition" in 2025 and 2026 where new AI-native business cohorts are launching faster and performing better than any previous group in the company’s history.

## Growth Metrics and the 2026 "Singularity"
* **Strong Financial Momentum:** Stripe grew 34% last year, a metric the founders attribute to the underlying growth of the businesses using the platform.
* **The 2026 "Singularity":** Patrick Collison noted that Q1 2026 may be remembered as the start of a "singularity" in the real economy. 
    * **Cohort Acceleration:** Businesses that signed up in 2025 and early 2026 are outperforming the 2023 and 2024 cohorts on a per-business basis.
    * **Phase Transition:** This shift isn't just "vibe-coded" hype; Stripe’s data shows a simultaneous increase in the number of new businesses and the median performance of those businesses.
* **Real Economy Health:** Despite market volatility over the last two years, Stripe’s time-series data suggests the broader economy is in robust shape, particularly for companies focused on innovation and retooling.

## The Infrastructure of Agentic Commerce
* **Evolution of Payments:** The founders anticipate a "torrent" of agentic commerce where AI agents, rather than humans, conduct transactions.
* **Tempo Incubation:** Stripe is incubating Tempo to address blockchain congestion. 
    * **High Throughput:** Future AI agents will require platforms capable of processing millions or billions of transactions per second, a scale no current payment rail supports.
    * **Stablecoin Synergy:** Stablecoins and high-throughput blockchains are viewed as the native currency and infrastructure for AI agents.
* **Unblocking the Web:** Because the current web is built for humans (e.g., CAPTCHAs), Stripe is doing the "boring" infrastructure work—API and protocol development—to make product catalogs from retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, and Etsy buyable directly within AI applications.

## AI Sentiment vs. Economic Reality
* **The Value Gap:** While some surveys suggest 80% of executives see no value in AI, John Collison dismissed this as "hogwash," arguing that the value is often hidden in layers of efficiency.
    * **Embedded Utility:** AI is already heavily integrated into high-value workflows like customer service augmentation and automated coding.
* **Bespoke Software:** Patrick predicts a fundamental shift where software becomes "like pizza"—cooked at the moment of consumption rather than mass-produced. 
    * **Shift in Economics:** Software is moving from a fixed-cost, infinitely monetized model to a regime involving inference costs and custom, real-time creation for the user.

## Strategic Philosophy and Long-term Compounding
* **Avoiding "MBA Brain":** John Collison argued against making product decisions based on generic TAM (Total Addressable Market) spreadsheets. 
    * **Specific Pain Points:** Stripe Atlas succeeded by solving the specific, granular frustrations of incorporation rather than following a theoretical business model.
* **The Power of Compounding:** Successes like Stripe Atlas and Stripe Press are described as a "long obedience in the same direction." 
    * **Stripe Press:** The publishing arm recently surpassed 1.1 million books sold, a milestone the founders view as "AGI-proof."
* **Legacy Transformation:** Incumbent firms are increasingly turning to Stripe when they decide to launch innovative or "retooling" projects, even if their core systems remain on legacy infrastructure.

> "I feel like there's at least a reasonable chance that 2026 Q1 will be looked back upon as the first quarter of the singularity... looking at real purchasing behavior on Stripe, end of '25, beginning of '26 is when I feel like we're really starting to see it." — **Patrick Collison**

> "You can't get too MBA brain about new products... you have to reason in product specifics. Any MBA would have told you that the adjacency of incorporation makes no sense... whereas you actually go talk to founders they're like, 'Guys, this is the single biggest issue I run into starting my company.'" — **John Collison**

> "Software historically has been created months, years beforehand and then freeze-dried... software should be like pizza in the sense that it should be cooked right then and there at the moment of use." — **Patrick Collison**

briefings.title: President Donald J. Trump’s 2026 State of the Union Address
briefings.tldr: President Trump declared the dawn of a "Golden Age" for America, citing a rapid one-year turnaround characterized by record-breaking economic growth, the total cessation of illegal border crossings, and major healthcare reforms ahead of the nation’s 250th anniversary.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
President Trump declared the dawn of a "Golden Age" for America, citing a rapid one-year turnaround characterized by record-breaking economic growth, the total cessation of illegal border crossings, and major healthcare reforms ahead of the nation’s 250th anniversary.

## Economic Growth and Financial Reform
*   **The "Trump Account" Program:** Announced tax-free investment accounts for American children, pre-funded by the U.S. Treasury and private donations.
    *   **Private Funding:** Noted that Michael and Susan Dell donated $6.25 billion to fund accounts for 25 million children.
    *   **Projected Growth:** These accounts are intended to grow to over $100,000 by the time a child turns 18.
*   **Tax Relief Initiatives:** Highlighted the passage of the "largest tax cuts in American history," focusing on the elimination of taxes for specific groups.
    *   **Eliminated Taxes:** No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, and no tax on Social Security for seniors.
    *   **Auto Loans:** Interest on auto loans is now tax-deductible for cars manufactured in the United States.
*   **Market Performance:** Reported that the Dow Jones surpassed 50,000 and the S&P reached 7,000, with 53 all-time record highs set since the election.
*   **Retirement Security:** Announced a new federal matching program for private-sector workers without retirement plans, offering up to $1,000 in matching contributions annually.

## Border Security and Public Safety
*   **Illegal Immigration:** Claimed a total cessation of illegal entries over the last nine months through the "strongest border in history."
    *   **Fentanyl Crisis:** Reported a record 56% decline in the flow of deadly fentanyl across the border within one year.
*   **National Crime Rates:** Cited the single largest decline in the murder rate in recorded history, with Washington D.C. reaching record-low crime levels following the deployment of federal law enforcement and the National Guard.
*   **Sanctuary Cities:** Called for an end to sanctuary city policies and the enactment of serious penalties for public officials who obstruct the removal of criminal aliens.
*   **Election Integrity:** Urged Congress to pass the **Save America Act**, which would mandate voter ID, proof of citizenship for voting, and the elimination of mail-in ballots except for specific exceptions (illness, disability, military, or travel).

## Healthcare and Consumer Protections
*   **Prescription Drug Costs:** Launched **TrumpRx.gov**, a platform implementing "Most Favored Nation" pricing to ensure Americans pay the lowest global prices for drugs.
    *   **Case Study:** Guest Catherine Rayner reportedly used the site to reduce an IVF drug's cost from $4,000 to under $500.
*   **Healthcare Insurance Reform:** Proposed a shift from paying insurance companies to giving subsidies directly to citizens to purchase their own healthcare.
*   **Housing Market:** Signed an executive order banning large Wall Street investment firms from purchasing single-family homes to protect the "American Dream" of homeownership for families like guest Rachel Wiggins.
*   **Ratepayer Protection Pledge:** Negotiated a deal requiring major tech companies to build their own power plants for AI data centers to prevent rising utility costs for the general public.

## National Defense and Global Diplomacy
*   **Middle East Operations:** Detailed "Operation Midnight Hammer," a military strike that reportedly obliterated Iran’s nuclear weapons program.
    *   **Hostage Returns:** Credited Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for negotiating the return of all 28 Israeli-American hostages (living and dead).
*   **Foreign Military Funding:** Announced that NATO countries have agreed to pay 5% of their GDP for military defense following strong U.S. requests.
*   **Military Recruitment and Benefits:** Noted a surge in recruitment across all branches and the issuance of a $1,776 "Warrior Dividend" to every service member, funded by tariff revenue.
*   **Global Conflict Resolution:** Claimed the administration has ended or mitigated eight wars, including conflicts between Kosovo and Serbia, and Armenia and Azerbaijan, while working to mediate peace between Russia and Ukraine.

> "Our nation is back, bigger, better, richer, and stronger than ever before... This is the golden age of America." — President Donald J. Trump

> "We are telling the major tech companies that they have the obligation to provide for their own power needs. They can build their own power plants... so that no one’s prices will go up." — President Donald J. Trump

> "I will never allow the world’s number one sponsor of terror to have a nuclear weapon. Can’t let that happen." — President Donald J. Trump

> "The revolution that began in 1776 has not ended. It still continues because the flame of liberty and independence still burns in the heart of every American patriot." — President Donald J. Trump
